## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect should be fixed: the README still documents the old 30-second default, so after this change users will be told the wrong timeout. The code change in `app/cli.py` is correct, and the updated `test_defaults` checks the new value. This review found no correctness or silent-failure defects in the code that changed.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cli.py:3 — comments — Once `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 60` lands, `README.md:3` is wrong: it still says "Requests time out after 30 seconds unless you pass `--timeout SECONDS`." The README's only job here is to describe the default this diff changes, and the diff does not update it. Fix: change `README.md:3` to say 60 seconds, so it matches `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT`. — Users reading the README will expect requests to fail after 30 seconds when they actually wait up to 60. That gives them a false picture when they tune `--timeout` or debug slow upstreams.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_cli.py:8` now asserts `args.timeout == 60` through `parse_args([])`. It tests the default users actually get, not the constant, so it would fail if the parser stopped using `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT`.
- The PR says an explicit `--timeout` still overrides the default. The existing test `test_explicit_options` (`tests/test_cli.py:13-16`) still checks this by passing `--timeout 12`.
